ranked_facts.why: The presence of a flat rod electroretinogram is more characteristic of Retinitis Pigmentosa and Enhanced S-cone Syndrome than Congenital Stationary Night Blindness, which typically presents with a normal or slightly reduced rod electroretinogram response.

The complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in the superotemporal region is more indicative of Retinitis Pigmentosa, which is characterized by progressive degeneration of the retina, than of Congenital Stationary Night Blindness or Enhanced S-cone Syndrome.
